Growth container fragments have been cleaned up... Processing...
This area has been cleaned. Waiting to execute the next cleaning plan in line.
What strange sounds...
Scary...
Ruan Mei's creation jumps onto the table!
(...Huh? What's that sound out there?)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Miss Ruan Mei is the very image of a scholar. I heard she once took a little vacation on a desert planet. By the time she left, she'd miraculously created a boom in the local ecology!
rows.speaker: Asta

rows.text: Anyway. What more needs to be said for someone smart enough to become Herta's research partner, hmm? Hurry up and head out, [Trailblazer]. See if you can find her.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Oink oink!
rows.speaker: Replicated Trotter

rows.text: Woof woof woof!
rows.speaker: Milk Almond Lifeform

rows.text: Eeep, eeep...
rows.speaker: Coriander Sesame Paste Lifeform

rows.text: Hehe!
rows.speaker: Replicated Phase Flame

rows.text: Of course. This is a summit between three geniuses.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Of course, go find her yourself. She borrowed the Phase Flame to do some research as soon as she got here — haven't seen a trace of her since.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: That's like asking "Is Herta a great person?" The answer is obvious!
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: I'm not sure, but she doesn't seem to get around much. She spends most of her time between the master control zone and the railway platform. Maybe you can start your search there?
rows.speaker: Asta

rows.text: The dessert was tasty. I would like more.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: You're so cute! Can I get an autograph?
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: I won't talk to you if you don't tell me why you're here.
rows.speaker: Department of Ecology Researcher

rows.text: ...Oh, that? You've got pretty good contacts if you know that already. The space station is a mess. Everyone's already swamped as it is, and now out of nowhere, there are a bunch of little creatures popping up.
rows.speaker: Department of Ecology Researcher

rows.text: I'll solve the space station's problems!
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: If you want to solve the problem, go check out the storage zone. Then you'll understand.
rows.speaker: Department of Ecology Researcher

rows.text: Yes... problems wrought by my own hand.
rows.speaker: Ruan Mei

rows.text: Does that bother you? I believe we will be able to be frank with each other, but that needs time.
rows.speaker: Ruan Mei

rows.text: Then I'll grant you even greater rewards.
rows.speaker: Ruan Mei

rows.text: When I first arrived on the space station, I borrowed the Phase Flame from Herta — it's an invention of member #29 Sserkal. I hoped to be enlightened by other Society members' results.
rows.speaker: Ruan Mei

rows.text: I do trust you.
rows.speaker: Ruan Mei

rows.text: This has nothing to do with them. Besides, the more people involved, the more problems there will be.
rows.speaker: Ruan Mei

rows.text: The researchers are still treating these entities as visitors... I want to steer clear of making my presence known, so as not to cause undue disturbances.
rows.speaker: Ruan Mei

rows.text: Alright, let's go.
rows.speaker: Ruan Mei

rows.text: Alright. There's no rush.
rows.speaker: Ruan Mei

rows.text: The Simulated Universe is my home!
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: It's probably an isolated glitch.
rows.speaker: Ruan Mei

rows.text: I was simply being overly cautious. It is a habit of mine. Apologies.
rows.speaker: Ruan Mei

rows.text: There are some things that I must tell you now. If I wait for the meeting to finish... then it might be too late.
rows.speaker: Ruan Mei

rows.text: There's much you don't know about the space station, and even more about Herta.
rows.speaker: Ruan Mei

rows.text: She gave me permission and said no more.
rows.speaker: Ruan Mei

rows.text: I'm giving you my access card. Give me your hand, and I'll input your fingerprint into it.
rows.speaker: Ruan Mei

rows.text: (Meow...)
rows.speaker: Ruan Mei's Creation

rows.text: (Meow...)
rows.speaker: Ruan Mei's Creation

rows.text: *sob*... *sob*
rows.speaker: Ruan Mei's Creation

rows.text: (*sob*... Ruan Mei... *sob*)
rows.speaker: Ruan Mei's Creation

rows.text: (*sob*... Ruan Mei... *sob*)
rows.speaker: Ruan Mei's Creation

rows.text: *sob*... *sob*
rows.speaker: Ruan Mei's Creation

rows.text: Over time, hidden truths tend to surface. Past traumas, which I'd rather leave behind, have made me skeptical about trusting anyone but myself.
rows.speaker: Ruan Mei

rows.text: Thank you.
rows.speaker: Ruan Mei

rows.text: I believe you.
rows.speaker: Ruan Mei

rows.text: Screwllum will stay on the space station for a while longer. He and Herta still have problems they need to solve. As for me, I'm leaving soon and won't bother with goodbyes.
rows.speaker: Ruan Mei

rows.text: ...I find that difficult to answer. I thank you, {F#Miss}{M#Mr.} Assistant.
rows.speaker: Ruan Mei

rows.text: Mm, I promise I will, {F#Miss}{M#Mr.} Assistant.
rows.speaker: Ruan Mei

rows.text: If fate allows and you're interested, upon our next meeting, we could journey to No Man's Land and traverse its tranquil glaciers...
rows.speaker: Ruan Mei

rows.text: Have you considered whether the answer to your question will be of any relevance to our current predicament?
I can't stand discourtesy — even when it comes from myself.
Because I can't bear to see idiots. Of course, they wouldn't want to see me either.
I can't stand discourtesy — even when it comes from myself.
The real "Ruan Mei's Creation" is hidden in the giant incubator below us.
Yes, I'm happy to meet you too. We've met before in the Simulated Universe.
rows.speaker: Ruan Mei

rows.text: Oh? Really?
rows.speaker: Ruan Mei

rows.text: I expect the views here had me lost in thought...
rows.speaker: Ruan Mei

rows.text: You don't like it? I worked very hard on it. You should at least have a try.
rows.speaker: Ruan Mei

rows.text: Delicious desserts remind people of how flowers look when they bloom. Ingest this dessert one bite at a time, and the sweetness will linger in your mouth.
rows.speaker: Ruan Mei

rows.text: No. My research area is short stories about toilets.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Let me get straight to the point. I think it's time to find another partner for the Simulated Universe.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Exactly as predicted: 56 seconds, on the dot.
rows.speaker: Ruan Mei

rows.text: How should I have explained it to you? I'm not good at communicating with others...
rows.speaker: Ruan Mei

rows.text: Restrained by time and place, its code of life could only be considered an incomplete attempt. I managed to replicate the moment it was born, however, it would soon disappear and be reduced to particles.
rows.speaker: Ruan Mei

rows.text: I did say that if a danger proved too great for you, I would personally step in to confront it.
rows.speaker: Ruan Mei

rows.text: Indeed, this is how I keep the distractions at bay. I have to admit that research once made me obsessive — that wasn't a good period in my life, though I now navigate it much more smoothly.
rows.speaker: Ruan Mei

rows.text: I do not have a life outside of research. People always think this price is unimaginable, but it seems rather acceptable to me.
rows.speaker: Ruan Mei

rows.text: I must admit, I'm not fond of scenarios where everything aligns perfectly with my expectations. An experiment should have its unforeseen twists.
rows.speaker: Ruan Mei

rows.text: Let's try again. Now, [Trailblazer], what else would you like to ask?
rows.speaker: Ruan Mei

rows.text: (Wh—Why can't I say what I want to say!?)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: You have quite the appetite. Alright, I'll give you the recipe.
rows.speaker: Ruan Mei

rows.text: Come and have a walk with me. A stroll is the most appropriate post-dessert activity.
rows.speaker: Ruan Mei

rows.text: My apologies, it appears my words have left you perplexed. Please, don't be on edge — I bear no ill will. I haven't interfered with your linguistic faculties — such an act would be impolite... I merely made a minor adjustment.
rows.speaker: Ruan Mei

rows.text: A few days ago, I made my interest in you known to Herta. My intention is for you to serve as an "assistant." Based on our interactions within the Simulated Universe, I firmly believe you fit the bill.
rows.speaker: Ruan Mei

rows.text: I find extending trust beyond myself is challenging. A single error in detailed research can generate issues, and I despise matters that escape my control.
rows.speaker: Ruan Mei

rows.text: Therefore, I added Anti-Truth Serum to this dessert. It will not harm you. However, you will be unable to say what you truly think when answering questions related to me.
rows.speaker: Ruan Mei

rows.text: Treat it as a layer of protection. This will shield my research and your personal safety. Once the problems have been dealt with, I'll give you the antidote.
rows.speaker: Ruan Mei

rows.text: I can also reward you as compensation for being my assistant. I will fulfill your every wish.
rows.speaker: Ruan Mei

rows.text: A surge of creativity led me to explore the cultivation of life on the space station.
rows.speaker: Ruan Mei

rows.text: In my imagination, these lifeforms would be a new variety that are born as geniuses. I planned to name them after Lambda, member #8 of the Genius Society...
rows.speaker: Ruan Mei

rows.text: I don't know where it went wrong. They possess their own sentience, but are nowhere near geniuses.
rows.speaker: Ruan Mei

rows.text: Moreover, my "free-range" approach seems to have backfired. In a lab leak incident a few days ago, some of these "little lifeforms" ran away and scattered all over the space station.
rows.speaker: Ruan Mei

rows.text: I do not wish for Herta or Asta to be involved in this. Therefore... I'm hoping you can assist in recovering these little lifeforms.
rows.speaker: Ruan Mei

rows.text: I entrust this to you. Once the little lifeforms are collected, simply find a proper place for them. The researchers in the Department of Ecology should know about this and provide you with suitable advice.
rows.speaker: Ruan Mei

rows.text: There is no need to tell me your answer. I just... felt like asking the question. How should I take care of them? Perhaps leaving them at the space station is the best choice.
rows.speaker: Ruan Mei

rows.text: Do I seem irresponsible? I'm sorry. I am often at a loss as to how to face my own creations.
rows.speaker: Ruan Mei

rows.text: The effects of the Anti-Truth Serum will also wear off. If others mention me to you in the future, you can answer however you like, or even pretend you never knew me.
rows.speaker: Ruan Mei

rows.text: After all, your memory of me will soon dissipate like smoke.
rows.speaker: Ruan Mei

rows.text: If I do not want a secret revealed, the most foolproof way is to destroy it. The Anti-Truth Serum will make you forget the brief period we spent together.
rows.speaker: Ruan Mei

rows.text: It won't take effect immediately. It is a slow, intangible process — like the sweet fragrance of lotus leaves, plum blossom, sticky rice, and frosting sugar.
rows.speaker: Ruan Mei

rows.text: Perhaps you will remember someone performed selfish experiments on the space station, but you will no longer remember their identity. Perhaps we will meet again someday, but you won't be able to connect me with the recollection.
rows.speaker: Ruan Mei

rows.text: That way, the connection between lifeforms will be erased. Friendships, secrets, grudges, lies, all will disappear.
rows.speaker: Ruan Mei

rows.text: It will make our lives... more relaxing.
rows.speaker: Ruan Mei

rows.text: Do you still remember the "No Man's Land" I mentioned? I'm considering a solo trip back there during my research downtime, just to see how things are.
rows.speaker: Ruan Mei

rows.text: I miss member #55, Yu Qingtu sometimes. She used to always make something delicious for me to drink every time we parted ways.
rows.speaker: Ruan Mei

rows.text: I hope I won't meet member #4 Polka Kakamond. That would be quite troublesome.
rows.speaker: Ruan Mei

rows.text: Who knows when the next gathering of geniuses will be? Do you have anything else you want to say to me, [Trailblazer]?
rows.speaker: Ruan Mei

rows.text: ...though I suppose it wouldn't be No Man's Land anymore... What a conundrum.
rows.speaker: Ruan Mei

rows.text: Hello. I hope I didn't startle you.
rows.speaker: Ruan Mei

rows.text: This is a work habit of mine — using touch to open my senses and letting the details of your biological existence flood into my brain helps me understand your construction as a living organism.
rows.speaker: Ruan Mei

rows.text: Such is the basis of deconstruction and reconstruction. Do not be concerned. You are very healthy — in fact, impeccably so. A perfect experimental specimen. I like perfect experimental specimens.
rows.speaker: Ruan Mei

rows.text: I don't usually go in and out of the space station, and only discovered today that it was blessed with such calm, open views. It is a wonderful fit for the sweet fragrance of lotus leaves, plum blossom, sticky rice, and frosting sugar.
rows.speaker: Ruan Mei

rows.text: Come here. Look, the blue planet is directly below us. It is so full of life. This dessert is very delicious. Here, take half.
rows.speaker: Ruan Mei

rows.text: I hope you like it too.
rows.speaker: Ruan Mei

rows.text: You ate Ruan Mei's snack.
So, what do you think? I can certainly prepare more for you. It's become somewhat of a tradition to bring strawberry pastries when I visit Stephen Lloyd. His attendance seems quite dependent on them.
rows.speaker: Ruan Mei

rows.text: Mmm, an outstanding dessert. Ten grams of cubed sugar, one dried and salt-preserved plum blossom. Baking and cooking are the same as nurturing a universe. The heat must be controlled, planning must be meticulous, and one must not panic... no matter what happens.
rows.speaker: Ruan Mei

rows.text: Unfortunately, there are still too many people in the space station. The clamor is not fitting for desserts. By the way...
rows.speaker: Ruan Mei

rows.text: [Trailblazer], do you remember what my "research" is about?
rows.speaker: Ruan Mei

rows.text: (What's going on... what am I... talking about?)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: I see. What a cute hobby.
rows.speaker: Ruan Mei

rows.text: But remember, the next time something like this happens it's crucial to mask your expression until you've ascertained the situation. If not...
rows.speaker: Ruan Mei

rows.text: ...you'll be full of weaknesses that others can see through.
rows.speaker: Ruan Mei

rows.text: The meeting of geniuses is over. As for the future of the Simulated Universe... That conclusion isn't important. What's important is your task.
rows.speaker: Ruan Mei

rows.text: You look... upset, correct? I regret my actions. There's no defending what I've done. Time and again, my experiments have fallen short, and they've always yielded predictable results.
rows.speaker: Ruan Mei

rows.text: I made a clone, but it... doesn't hold a candle to the Emanator.
rows.speaker: Ruan Mei

rows.text: Like every living being, it inevitably faced its demise as it journeyed towards the end — I find no fault in that.
rows.speaker: Ruan Mei

rows.text: However, even the briefest life should have meaning. I want to know the limits of its capacity. It will indicate how far I've gone in a field completely incomprehensible to me.
rows.speaker: Ruan Mei

rows.text: Haha, and it was "a minuscule step" — just as I had predicted.
rows.speaker: Ruan Mei

rows.text: That's where the joy lies. Even the most predictable storylines can have their pleasant surprises.
rows.speaker: Ruan Mei

rows.text: Ahh, that's right. They're called heliobi. I guess you could say that wubbaboos and heliobi are sort of like cousins — both are types of energy lifeform.
rows.speaker: Adler

rows.text: (Spontaneous combustion of the human body... that is most likely the truth.)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: ...Probably running errands for Herta?
...Listening to Asta complain?
...Walking the dog with Arlan?
A portrait of internal turmoil. You look troubled. Do you need help?
rows.speaker: Dr. Ratio

rows.text: Do try to think for yourself.
rows.speaker: Dr. Ratio

rows.text: (Let me remember my initial conversation with Herta, just in case...)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Let me describe it again, in case you forgot: It's an energy lifeform. It's alive, but it doesn't have a body.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Energy lifeform?
That's not the point. I wouldn't be bothering with it if it didn't have something to do with the Genius Society.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: So, to sum it up, the last time you laid eyes on Herta was in her office. She sent you on a wild goose chase for some trinket, the Curio, after which you knew nothing else until Lady Asta contacted you.
rows.speaker: Dr. Ratio

rows.text: I will head to Herta's office and activate the folded space in the Curio storage room. With some changes to its parameters, I can use it to block the fire's teleportation routes and seal it inside the station.
rows.speaker: Screwllum

rows.text: Mr. Ratio, please go with {F#Miss}{M#Mr.} [Trailblazer] and contain the fire.
rows.speaker: Screwllum

rows.text: I don't know. That depends on your friend.
rows.speaker: Dr. Ratio

rows.text: If that's the narrative you're sticking to, then indulge me: Who, pray tell, can substantiate this captivating drama?
rows.speaker: Dr. Ratio

rows.text: A second-hand account, she wasn't at the scene. Hearsay hardly counts as compelling evidence, now, does it?
rows.speaker: Dr. Ratio

rows.text: Apologies. Herta did not mention this to me.
rows.speaker: Screwllum

rows.text: Affirmation: We can ask Herta herself.
rows.speaker: Screwllum

rows.text: Mr. Ratio, your style of questioning would seem to have a preconceived bias.
rows.speaker: Screwllum

rows.text: Apologies, it's an unfortunate habit of mine. When one is immersed in academic research, skepticism comes far more naturally than belief.
rows.speaker: Dr. Ratio

rows.text: It is also the most efficient method, judging from my experience — seeking answers with a negative hypothesis in mind is still valid research. It can still help us reach the truth.
rows.speaker: Dr. Ratio

rows.text: ...If these two incidents were caused by the same person, then the suspicion put on you would decrease... provided that this fire-suppression record does exist in the system.
rows.speaker: Dr. Ratio

rows.text: We'll see in the main control room. Let's go... Huh? What was that?
rows.speaker: Asta

rows.text: This is...
rows.speaker: Asta

rows.text: This business is over, and I believe the space station will be able to deal with any internal aftershocks. In Herta's stead, I thank for your efforts, {F#Madam}{M#Sir}.
rows.speaker: Screwllum

rows.text: A declaration of war and an announcement of what's to come — they have set their sights on you. The Legion's impact remains, and the Annihilation Gang is already paying a visit. It almost seems like this space station is more suited for the Path of Destruction than Erudition.
rows.speaker: Dr. Ratio

rows.text: This "Duke Inferno," Ifrit, is a lifeform that hails from Fetora — a world long since destroyed. His race, the ever-burning fire demons, regard Nanook as their emperor and savior, but the Aeon has never cast their gaze upon them.
rows.speaker: Screwllum

rows.text: Don't play the fool. Think.
rows.speaker: Dr. Ratio

rows.text: A group of pitiful lunatics. I like Dr. Primitive's assessment of them: "The value Nanook sees in the Annihilation Gang is perhaps far less than what one might see in a child who deliberately broke a vase."
rows.speaker: Dr. Ratio

rows.text: The fire demons have a cruel temper and instinctively ignite and destroy items. Ifrit is particularly evil and cruel, even among his kin. The Ever-Flame Mansion he heads is even the archenemy of the Jepella Brotherhood, despite both groups belonging to the Annihilation Gang.
rows.speaker: Dr. Ratio

rows.text: Jepella Brotherhood... I've heard that name somewhere...
rows.speaker: Asta

rows.text: On the Stellaron Hunters' wanted posters, they stand accused of inciting the Jepella Rebellion — the uprising that caused the downfall of the Brotherhood.
rows.speaker: Screwllum

rows.text: The Jepella Palace crumbled in the scorching flames, and Ifrit's power has grown by the day ever since. Would you believe it to be merely a coincidence?
rows.speaker: Dr. Ratio

rows.text: Something similar is about to happen here. Spontaneous combustion? For him, it's as routine as me finding fault in everything. The disappearance of researchers and the puppet were all part of the plan. And after that...
rows.speaker: Dr. Ratio

rows.text: That video will soon circulate, and this station's fate? Flames, nothing but flames.
rows.speaker: Dr. Ratio

rows.text: The destruction of "trust."
rows.speaker: Screwllum

rows.text: I'm afraid more than trust will be destroyed here.
rows.speaker: Dr. Ratio

rows.text: We need to start acting now if you want to survive. You — come with me.
rows.speaker: Dr. Ratio

rows.text: You have a superior strategy? Pray tell. Do we set the two of them loose, turning whispered fears into full-blown pandemonium?
rows.speaker: Dr. Ratio

rows.text: If we did that, we'd be at a disadvantage... I'll stay here and try to contain the news as best I can. Please investigate the issue quickly.
rows.speaker: Asta

rows.text: What else do you need me to do?
rows.speaker: Arlan

rows.text: Take me to the one who knows the most about Curios within the Department of Ecology, if you would be so kind.
rows.speaker: Dr. Ratio

rows.text: H—He disappeared too...
rows.speaker: Arlan

rows.text: I didn't really notice at first — Adler's difficult to get a hold of at the best of times...
rows.speaker: Arlan

rows.text: ...but it's been a few system hours, and I still can't reach him. Even the surveillance cameras can't find any trace...
rows.speaker: Arlan

rows.text: The last time I saw him was in the master control zone. He was with Wen Shiling from the Department of Implement Arts.
rows.speaker: Arlan

rows.text: Lead the way. You said Adler was on the verge of a discovery, yet couldn't confer his knowledge. Intriguing and frustrating, to say the least.
rows.speaker: Dr. Ratio

rows.text: If his disappearance is also related to the case here, then maybe he really did stumble upon something important.
rows.speaker: Dr. Ratio

rows.text: (True... the keywords that got Adler thinking were "Energy Lifeforms." Duke Inferno is also an energy lifeform. Coincidence?)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: (We need to investigate this...)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Oh, it's you! It's Adler... Adler disappeared! *sob*
rows.speaker: Wen Shiling

rows.text: Adler, he... he disappeared... *sob*
rows.speaker: Wen Shiling

rows.text: H—He's been acting really weird recently — always researching stuff like spontaneous combustion, supernatural activities...
rows.speaker: Wen Shiling

rows.text: Who said I want him back!?
rows.speaker: Wen Shiling

rows.text: Your countenance suggests tragedy.
rows.speaker: Dr. Ratio

rows.text: So the researchers who disappeared were at the forefront of challenging management. Isn't that a curious puzzle piece?
rows.speaker: Dr. Ratio

rows.text: I finished browsing through this booklet while you were replying to messages. It recorded the lives of a few Genius Society members — I'd say it contains some interesting information.
rows.speaker: Dr. Ratio

rows.text: It's time to go back and chat with Lady Asta and Mr. Screwllum.
rows.speaker: Dr. Ratio

rows.text: You're back.
rows.speaker: Asta

rows.text: I've been monitoring the Dark Web — I barely managed to stop the video from spreading. The incident hasn't grown any bigger — for now. How are things with you?
rows.speaker: Asta

rows.text: Less than promising, or to use a different phrase — we're in deep trouble.
rows.speaker: Dr. Ratio

rows.text: We're running out of time, let's retrace our steps and evaluate the situation. From the data we've collected, there are three avenues we can explore...
rows.speaker: Dr. Ratio

rows.text: We don't know where the victims went, but Duke Inferno's plan is now clear.
rows.speaker: Dr. Ratio

rows.text: And the sudden and consecutive disappearances provided the best environment for chaos to fester.
rows.speaker: Dr. Ratio

rows.text: Once the seed of unrest has sprouted, he will then send out an announcement for an imminent attack. It will push the crisis from the dark into the light, catalyzing it into new growth and bloom.
rows.speaker: Dr. Ratio

rows.text: The next step would be to ignite the spark. Look at those researchers who disappeared — what would happen if someone realized their similarities? I need say no more.
rows.speaker: Dr. Ratio

rows.text: It was all a premeditated trap to stir up chaos on the space station!
rows.speaker: Asta

rows.text: I will head to Herta's office and activate the folded space in the Curio storage room. With some changes to its parameters, I can use it to block the fire's teleportation routes and seal it inside the station.
rows.speaker: Screwllum

rows.text: Mr. Ratio, please go with {F#Miss}{M#Mr.} [Trailblazer] and contain the fire.
rows.speaker: Screwllum

rows.text: ...We're running out of time.
rows.speaker: Dr. Ratio

rows.text: Th—This...
rows.speaker: Asta

rows.text: ...No. It isn't enough.
rows.speaker: Screwllum

rows.text: Indeed. It needs one more spark.
rows.speaker: Dr. Ratio

rows.text: What do you mean?
rows.speaker: Asta

rows.text: If you limit your involvement to this, there's still room for excuses. If it were me...
rows.speaker: Dr. Ratio

rows.text: ...I wouldn't give you the chance.
rows.speaker: Dr. Ratio

rows.text: {F#Miss}{M#Mr.} [Trailblazer], you must have many questions. Please be patient, Asta will explain it all to you.
rows.speaker: Screwllum

rows.text: Stay calm. Asta was merely teleported — her life was not in danger.
rows.speaker: Screwllum

rows.text: Based on firsthand experience, I have ascertained that Ifrit's flame is simply a splinter of the primordial Phase Flame — lacking any phase-shift ability. Logic: Asta is still within the confines of the space station.
rows.speaker: Screwllum

rows.text: That flame must still be somewhere inside the station. Find it, and we'll find a way to bring her back.
rows.speaker: Dr. Ratio

rows.text: Hahaha... a splinter, you say? The arrogance of the gifted is charming, in its own way.
Try then, if you must.

It seems that Duke Inferno didn't deign to personally grace the space station. He merely cast infernal fire into our midst to wreak havoc among the researchers. When the fire fizzles out, his malevolent plans will vanish without a trace.
rows.speaker: Dr. Ratio

rows.text: The way is awash with flames! It must have just teleported!
rows.speaker: Dr. Ratio

rows.text: Excuse me, [Trailblazer], tell me — what were you doing the last time you saw that puppet?
rows.speaker: Dr. Ratio

rows.text: Don't play the fool. Think.
rows.speaker: Dr. Ratio

rows.text: Don't play the fool. Think.
rows.speaker: Dr. Ratio

rows.text: I commend your stamina for recounting that interminable tale — you must be exhausted. My ears certainly are.
rows.speaker: Dr. Ratio

rows.text: Be careful — get ready to dash into the fire.
rows.speaker: Dr. Ratio

rows.text: It's over.
rows.speaker: Dr. Ratio

rows.text: Well, if you lace up those boots and start sprinting now, you might just catch the IPC shuttle in four system hours. But as it stands, not a single soul can corroborate {F#her}{M#his} story.
rows.speaker: Dr. Ratio

rows.text: Ignorant fools blindly chasing the firelight — not knowing that the blessings of Destruction already lie at their feet.
It is little wonder that even the descent of the savior's Legion was unable to cleanse this place. I will acknowledge my brashness... for now.
But next time, expect no intermediaries. I will come to personally offer you the demise of your sins with infernal fire.
If {F#she}{M#he} is truly innocent, {F#she}{M#he} can clear {F#her}{M#his} name with answers.
rows.speaker: Dr. Ratio

rows.text: The small fragment of consciousness in there is gone. Duke Inferno has discarded this fire...
rows.speaker: Dr. Ratio

rows.text: ...Oh? No. Hold on...
rows.speaker: Dr. Ratio

rows.text: Good work. You did very well.
rows.speaker: Screwllum

rows.text: Rest assured, Asta only had a fright. She is recovering in the Clinic.
rows.speaker: Screwllum

rows.text: While you were chasing the enemy, the Security Department also found the missing researchers. Affirmation: They are all safe and sound.
rows.speaker: Screwllum

rows.text: It was all thanks to Adler.
rows.speaker: Screwllum

rows.text: They fell into a spatial Curio and could not leave until the Department of Ecology's most knowledgeable Curio expert solved it from within.
rows.speaker: Screwllum

rows.text: Many of them were shaken by their experience when Arlan found them, but they are otherwise fine.
rows.speaker: Screwllum

rows.text: Yes. It is over.
rows.speaker: Screwllum

rows.text: But there is one mystery that remains unsolved...
rows.speaker: Screwllum

rows.text: Haha, and that is something I must deal with myself.
rows.speaker: Screwllum

rows.text: Fallout from this incident remains. Surely you have plenty of pressing matters to attend to? Or is the safety of the space station beneath your concern?
rows.speaker: Dr. Ratio

rows.text: Answer: That is exactly why I came. After all, the principal figure in this whole affair... is right here.
rows.speaker: Screwllum

rows.text: Haha... When did you start to doubt me?
rows.speaker: Dr. Ratio

rows.text: "When one is immersed in academic research, skepticism comes far more naturally than belief."
rows.speaker: Screwllum

rows.text: I've had the same bad habit as you since the beginning, Mr. Ratio.
rows.speaker: Screwllum

rows.text: I must say, I'm quite honored, Mr. Screwllum, but do explain — why opt for silent wisdom when you already had the pieces of the puzzle?
rows.speaker: Dr. Ratio

rows.text: For curiosity's sake. Affirmation: I made the same decision as you. To accompany and observe.
rows.speaker: Screwllum

rows.text: Oh... and when did you become convinced?
rows.speaker: Dr. Ratio

rows.text: Objectively speaking, aside from some minor spiritual trauma, no researchers were hurt in this attack... which never aligned with the Annihilation Gang's modus operandi.
rows.speaker: Screwllum

rows.text: Logic: A third party saved them.
rows.speaker: Screwllum

rows.text: Had I not fortuitously acquired a spark of the Phase Flame and intervened in Duke Inferno's teleportation, those people would already be space waste — floating past the windows here.
rows.speaker: Dr. Ratio

rows.text: You are more candid than I calculated.
rows.speaker: Screwllum

rows.text: But still behaving within your calculations, no?
rows.speaker: Dr. Ratio

rows.text: One last question. Screwllum, genius though you are, can you deduce why I did this?
rows.speaker: Dr. Ratio

rows.text: I cannot be sure. I can only hypothesize. Helping the weak hints at the merciful instinct of a medical doctor, but maintaining a cool, detached observation reveals the strictness of a scholar...
rows.speaker: Screwllum

rows.text: ...and pulling the strings from behind the curtain is akin to laying down the gauntlet to a genius.
rows.speaker: Screwllum

rows.text: The ruler of Planet Screwllum is indeed well-versed in the human mind. It's a pity you are as much in the ivory tower as other geniuses — you still got one thing wrong.
rows.speaker: Dr. Ratio

rows.text: To stand aside and observe is the best treatment one can give. There is a disease called "foolishness" that is harder to cure than any ailment.
rows.speaker: Dr. Ratio

rows.text: The Path of Erudition has neither reason nor logic. While geniuses wander among the stars, the ordinary can't even trace their footsteps. Those less gifted have no choice but to walk alone, enduring a lifetime of tumbles and triumphs...
rows.speaker: Dr. Ratio

rows.text: ...but even a life marked by failure is a life worth living — it is only in moments of solitude and despair, when help is absent, that fools grasp how to pick themselves up.
rows.speaker: Dr. Ratio

rows.text: I have a fastidious nature — I cannot stand fools, idiots, or imbeciles. Seeing them fills me with dread. Regrettably, this space station is just like the Intelligentsia Guild — devoid of geniuses and filled with mediocrity.
rows.speaker: Dr. Ratio

rows.text: You wish to uproot the researchers' blind worship of geniuses.
rows.speaker: Screwllum

rows.text: I am only laying out my questions. As for the answers... They'll find them themselves.
rows.speaker: Dr. Ratio

rows.text: Pursuit tinged with negativity is still pursuit, and it is capable of leading us to the right conclusion. For the masses of the mediocre to reach a level of awareness — this is a necessary rite of passage.
rows.speaker: Dr. Ratio

rows.text: You are indeed more like a "medical doctor" than a scholar.
rows.speaker: Screwllum

rows.text: As for the spark I leave behind...
rows.speaker: Dr. Ratio

rows.text: I believe Asta will deal with it properly.
rows.speaker: Screwllum

rows.text: It is also a lesson I left for her.
rows.speaker: Dr. Ratio

rows.text: With that, I take my leave. I look forward to future encounters with such brilliant minds. Let's hope they're as memorable as those we had today.
rows.speaker: Dr. Ratio

rows.text: It appears I was overthinking things. Impulsive behavior is pretty characteristic of her after all.
rows.speaker: Ruan Mei

rows.text: Why hasn't Ruan Mei come?
The air in the space station has a pleasant quality. Affirmation: Knowledge flows within it.
rows.speaker: Screwllum

rows.text: Will there be a fifth genius joining?
We anticipate the inclusion of a different perspective. I await our esteemed guest and shall offer the highest courtesies — I'm confident that our discussions will generate illuminating insights.
rows.speaker: Screwllum

rows.text: I want to know about member #64, Dr. Primitive.

Dr. Primitive's true identity is not known to me. His previous transgressions against humanity lead some to conclude he may be an inorganic entity. Affirmation: All beings, organic or otherwise, should value peace.
rows.speaker: Screwllum

rows.text: How long will you be staying on the space station?
I will stay for a while longer. Lady Asta has recently expressed concerns regarding disturbances on the space station. Conclusion: Extended observation is necessary.
rows.speaker: Screwllum

rows.text: Yes.
The Simulated Universe is my home!
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: No.
It's probably an isolated glitch.
rows.speaker: Ruan Mei

rows.text: I didn't end up saying anything.
I was simply being overly cautious. It is a habit of mine. Apologies.
rows.speaker: Ruan Mei

rows.text: Is there something I shouldn't hear?
No. You misunderstand. While Herta is tied up in meetings, you might find it more convenient to roam the space station.
rows.speaker: Ruan Mei

rows.text: There are some things that I must tell you now. If I wait for the meeting to finish... then it might be too late.
rows.speaker: Ruan Mei

rows.text: There are other zones in the space station?
There's much you don't know about the space station, and even more about Herta.
rows.speaker: Ruan Mei

rows.text: So Herta gave you permission to use this place?
She gave me permission and said no more.
rows.speaker: Ruan Mei

rows.text: I'm giving you my access card. Give me your hand, and I'll input your fingerprint into it.
rows.speaker: Ruan Mei

rows.text: (Cheer passionately)
(Bow politely)
Let me get straight to the point. I think it's time to find another partner for the Simulated Universe.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Hi, Ruan Mei, I've been waiting for you. Oh, you're here too? Looks like you two have become quite friendly.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: It's good to see you, {F#madam}{M#sir}. Affirmation: This reunion has happened earlier than my calculations predicted.
rows.speaker: Screwllum

rows.text: Though you weren't invited, I welcome you to remember this historical moment, [Trailblazer]. How long has it been since three geniuses were in the same room together? And how long will we have to wait for it to happen again?
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Affirmative. Discounting our discussions on the Simulated Universe, our interactions are scarce. I look forward to the innovative ideas that may emerge from this juxtaposition of minds.
rows.speaker: Screwllum

rows.text: ...You wish to kick Stephen out?
rows.speaker: Ruan Mei

rows.text: No, of course not! Stephen doesn't want to get involved and voted to abstain — whatever. Look, I respect the way people want to live, but he doesn't have the chance to be involved in this decision-making anymore.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Question: Are we introducing a fifth partner for the Simulated Universe?
rows.speaker: Screwllum

rows.text: Yes. A fifth genius.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: The reason for our gathering is clear to everyone present. What else could prompt such a gathering of brilliant minds except for the "answer"?
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: No one can refuse the secret of the Aeons, not even Zandar. We'll definitely get a response.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: What if the responder is Polka Kakamond?
rows.speaker: Ruan Mei

rows.text: That'd be great! Hey, Lord of Silence, are you listening? I'm member #83, Herta, and I want to meet you. I believe you and I will have a lot to talk about.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: It's unlikely we'll hear from Polka Kakamond. She's been off the grid for quite some time.
rows.speaker: Screwllum

rows.text: Probability: Member #64, Dr. Primitive, may appear.
rows.speaker: Screwllum

rows.text: That's a hard pass. Given Dr. Primitive's shady research practices and his tussle with the Galaxy Rangers, the IPC will surely turn this into a media circus... he can get lost. I'd prefer it if the Simulated Universe remained scandal-free.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: What about Yu Qingtu? Are you still in touch with her, Ruan Mei? Is she still alive?
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: ...Can we ask {F#her}{M#him} to leave if we are to discuss this topic? The process will be long... and boring. There's no need to take up other people's time.
rows.speaker: Ruan Mei

rows.text: Of course. You brought {F#her}{M#him} in, after all. It's up to you.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Alright, let me walk you out.
rows.speaker: Ruan Mei

rows.text: Reuniting under such conditions... Affirmation: Unpleasant.
rows.speaker: Screwllum

rows.text: Don't worry. We're just ticking the boxes to understand what happened. You don't really think we suspect you, right?
rows.speaker: Asta

rows.text: Just me?
What do you have in mind?
Who got you so upset?
What did Adler do to you?
We'll get him back.
(Recount Pamela's findings.)
How is Asta?
How did you find them?
Is it over?
Why do I feel like you didn't do much...?
